cleanIntro: The METE SFT's field strip is NOT the same motion as the older TP9 books, and the difference is worth knowing before you start: here the slide moves forward only about 0.6 inch and then LIFTS UP off the frame, and it goes back on by being pressed down at that same 0.6 inch offset and pushed rearward. Everything else is the familiar Canik sequence — unload, press the trigger to drop the striker, both takedown catches down. The red striker indicator disappearing is your confirmation. If your barrel is threaded the muzzle protector must come off first, and the whole Suppressor Ready Models chapter is scoped to suppressed models only.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber confirmed empty
steps.action: Point the pistol somewhere safe, drop the magazine and confirm the chamber is empty by following the Unloading section — Canik references it by name at the head of every disassembly instruction in this book rather than repeating it. Clear the bench of live ammunition, loaded magazines and any other firearm before you start.
steps.prose: This is a striker gun with no manual safety. The chamber check is the whole of your margin.
steps.quote: 1. Before beginning, remove all live ammunition, loaded magazines and other firearms from the working area. Remove the magazine from the pistol. To do so, follow the procedures detailed in the, Unloading the Pistol section and confirm the chamber is empty.

steps.title: Threaded barrel? The protector comes off first
steps.action: If your METE SFT has a threaded muzzle, the thread protector must come off before disassembly — Canik puts that as a warning at the head of the disassembly section. Use the wrench from the case, and note the direction: on a metric left-hand barrel you unscrew CLOCKWISE. If your barrel is not threaded, this section does not apply to your pistol at all.
steps.prose: Thread pitch varies between metric and inch configurations, so read the barrel rather than assuming.
steps.caution: WARNING! Threaded muzzle protector must be taken off before disassembly.
steps.quote: Notice! This section only applies to threaded barrel configurations.

steps.title: Secure the pistol, drop the striker
steps.action: Rest the unloaded pistol firmly on your lap or a table, muzzle in a safe direction, and press the trigger to lower the striker. The red striker indicator disappearing is how you know it is down, and the takedown catches will not release the slide until it is. Put eye protection on before the next step.
steps.prose: Support the gun rather than holding it up. The catch pull needs two hands working against each other.
steps.quote: 1. While remembering to maintain a safe muzzle direction, secure the unloaded pistol firmly in a supported location such as your lap, or on a table. Pull the trigger to lower the striker. Note: When the striker is lowered, the red striker indicator is not visible. (See lllustration #7)

steps.title: 0.6 inch forward, then LIFT the slide off
steps.action: Hold the pistol in your primary hand and pull both takedown catches above the trigger down with the index finger and thumb of your other hand, while pushing the slide forward with your primary thumb. The slide only travels about 0.6 inch — do not expect it to run off the front. At that point lift the slide UP until it is free of the frame.
steps.prose: This is where owners of older Canik pistols get stuck: they keep pushing forward and the slide will not go, because on this model it comes off vertically.
steps.caution: About 0.6 inch forward, then lift. Not forward off the front.
steps.quote: 2. While holding the pistol in your primary hand, grasp the take down catches, located above the trigger. Pull them down using index finger and thumb of your secondary hand. At the same time using the thumb of your primary hand push the slide forward. (See lllustration #9 and #10) (Please note the slide will only move forward about 0.6 inch) Lift the slide up until it is free of frame. (lllustration #11)

steps.title: Recoil spring out, barrel out
steps.action: Hold the slide upside down. Push the recoil spring toward the muzzle to unseat it and lift it free. Then lift the barrel slightly, push it forward toward the muzzle, and pull it back and up out of the slide. Four parts on the bench: frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring.
steps.prose: The spring is captive as an assembly but still under load until it clears its seat.
steps.aside: 2. Lift the barrel slightly and push it forward toward the muzzle. Then you can pull it back and lift it free from the slide.
steps.quote: 1. Holding the slide with primary hand, use your secondary hand to push the recoil spring toward the muzzle and lift it free. (See lllustration #12)

steps.title: Bore from the chamber to the muzzle
steps.action: Attach the correct calibre nylon bore brush to the rod, dampen it with CLP and push and pull it through the barrel several times from the CHAMBER to the MUZZLE. Then swap to a cloth patch on the rod and push it through several times to carry the loosened fouling out. Repeat until a patch comes out clean, then leave a light coating of CLP in the bore.
steps.prose: Chamber-to-muzzle keeps the brush off the crown and moves fouling the way the bullet went.
steps.aside: Repeat this process with the brush and cleaning patches until a final patch comes out clean after swabbing the bore.
steps.quote: 4. Dampen the screw-in nylon bore brush with cleaner, lubricant, protectant (CLP) and then push/pull the brush through the barrel several times from the chamber to the muzzle.

steps.title: Where the CLP actually goes
steps.action: Take the shooting residue off the slide, the barrel exterior and the action parts with the brush and cloth, then put a light coat of CLP on a specific short list: the frame rails, the trigger bar, the inside of the ejector assembly, the rails on the slide, the firing pin block, and the slide's inner surface where the barrel rides. Everywhere else gets wiped, not oiled.
steps.prose: That list is Canik's, and it is short on purpose. A striker gun with oil everywhere collects grit in the frame.
steps.quote: 7. Remove shooting residue from the slide, barrel's exterior, and action parts using the brush and cloth supplied. Apply a light coating of CLP to the rails, trigger bar and inside of the ejector assembly of frame and rails on the slide and firing pin block together with the slide's inner side where the barrel operates.

steps.title: Nothing abrasive, ever
steps.action: Do not take sandpaper or emery cloth to any part of this pistol. Canik's reasoning is mechanical rather than cosmetic: anything more aggressive than a Scotch Brite damages the precision contact surfaces, and a damaged contact surface creates friction, and friction on a striker pistol is a malfunction. Solvents go in a well-ventilated area away from open flames.
steps.prose: This bites people trying to polish a feed ramp or scrub a stubborn carbon ring off the breech face.
steps.quote: WARNING! MAINTAINING THE FINISH ON YOUR PISTOL Do not use sandpaper or emery cloth to clean any part of the firearm or suppressor. Abrasives more aggressive than Scotch Brite may damage the precision contact surfaces of the pistol, resulting in friction that can lead to malfunctions of the firearm and suppressor.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring. The disassembly chapter ends there and Canik publishes nothing deeper for the METE SFT. Going back together is the reverse — and remember the 0.6 inch: the slide is pressed onto the frame at that offset from the rear and then pushed rearward.
steps.prose: Anything beyond this is not published by Canik for this pistol.
steps.quote: 3. Align the slide cutouts with frame rails. Press slide onto the frame which is about 0.6" distance from the rear. Push the slide rearward. (See Illustration #16a)

deepAbsentReason: Canik publishes NO deeper procedure for this pistol. The book's Disassembly chapter consists of exactly two steps — recoil spring out and barrel out — and stops. Every other teardown in the manual is an accessory or configuration job scoped by the manual itself: the thread protector ('this section only applies to threaded barrel configurations'), the optic sight interface and its lid, the magazine release button extensions, the backstrap, and the Suppressor Ready Models chapter ('this section is for suppressed models only'). None of them is a deeper clean of the pistol, so there is nothing published to walk. Canik also warns that any part installed other than a CANiK Accessory Program part voids the warranty and may damage the pistol, and that failure to follow the disassembly and assembly instructions may damage it — inventing a striker or fire-control teardown here would be substitution.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Correct calibre nylon bore brush on the rod, dampened with CLP
Push/pull through the barrel several times from the CHAMBER to the MUZZLE
Cloth patches on the rod until a final patch comes out clean
Light coating of CLP left in the bore

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Brush and cloth to take shooting residue off the slide and the barrel exterior
Light CLP on the slide rails, the firing pin block, and the inner surface where the barrel operates
Nothing abrasive — no sandpaper, no emery cloth

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Residue off the action parts with the supplied brush and cloth
Light CLP on the frame rails, the trigger bar and inside the ejector assembly
Wipe the outer surfaces with a soft cloth dipped in good quality gun oil

cleaning.name: OPTIC LID & THREADED MODELS
tasks: Optic sight lid: T10 Torx on the lid screws; NEVER pry the lid off
If the lid is tight, remove the slide first and push it up through the screw hole with the Torx key
Threaded barrels: muzzle protector off before disassembly
Suppressed models: standard pressure only, and no lead, frangible or pre-fragmented ammunition

reassembly: Hold the slide muzzle-down, drop the barrel in, then turn the slide muzzle-up so the barrel settles into place.
Put the recoil spring into the muzzle end of the slide with its FLAT end facing the chamber, and press it toward the muzzle and slightly down.
Align the slide cutouts with the frame rails and press the slide down onto the frame at about 0.6 inch from the rear.
Push the slide rearward until it seats and the takedown catches rise.
Rack the slide to confirm it is correctly assembled.
If the barrel is threaded, refit the thread protector — metric left-hand barrels tighten ANTICLOCKWISE.
fncheck: With the pistol empty, rack the slide fully and let it go forward under its own spring rather than riding it, and confirm it returns to battery every time. Check the takedown catches have risen back into place — a slide that is on but not latched will come off under recoil. Press the trigger and confirm it breaks and then resets when the slide is cycled, and check the red striker indicator appears when the striker is cocked and disappears when it is down. Finally seat an empty magazine and confirm the slide locks back.
